Reproducing Kalogriopoulos, Tei et al. (2024) from dandiset 001354¶

Paper. Kalogriopoulos NA, Tei R, Yan Y, Klein PM, Ravalin M, Cai B, Soltesz I, Li Y, Ting AY (2024). Synthetic GPCRs for programmable sensing and control of cell behaviour. Nature 637, 230-239. doi:10.1038/s41586-024-08282-3. The claims file (claims/kalogriopoulos-2024.yaml) was written from the version of record as served by Europe PMC (PMC11666456, marked "corrected publication 2025") with its Supplementary Information.

Dandiset. DANDI:001354, version 0.250312.0036 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001354/0.250312.0036). The paper does not cite the dandiset or any version of it (its Data availability says no separate datasets were generated). The archive has one published version, 0.250312.0036, and a draft with the same 50 assets and the same size; the published version is pinned, as the most recent published one. The dandiset holds the acute slice recordings of Fig. 4e-j and Extended Data Fig. 12a-h: whole-cell current clamp of CA1 neurons expressing anti-mCherry PAGER-Gi, one NWB file per cell.

What can be tested. Every NWB file is read below. The files hold the voltage and the injected current of every sweep, with the subject, the date and the cell, but no record of which cells received DCZ alone and which DCZ plus mCherry, of when DCZ was applied, of each cell's mEGFP intensity, or of the mCherry preincubation time. The slice claims compare the two conditions around the DCZ onset, so none of them can be tested; the other 24 claims are on culture, imaging and biochemical data that the dandiset does not hold. The notebook checks the data against the paper's description and computes the paper's per-sweep measures and exclusions for all cells, so that the counts the paper gives can be set against the files.

import resource
import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from dandi.dandiapi import DandiAPIClient

import pager_slice as ps

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)

started = time.time()
cells, sweeps = ps.load_all(workers=4)
print(f"loaded {len(cells)} files, {len(sweeps)} sweeps from dandiset {ps.DANDISET_ID} "
      f"version {ps.DANDISET_VERSION} in {time.time() - started:.0f} s; "
      f"peak memory {resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1e6:.2f} GB")

The archive's summary (8 subjects, 50 cells) agrees with the files: 8 mice, all female (as the Methods state), 50 cells, each in its own file and with its own slice id. The paper counts 15 cells from 7 mice with DCZ and 26 cells from 6 mice with DCZ plus mCherry: 41 cells, and 13 mice if no mouse gave cells to both groups. The files hold 9 cells more, and 8 mice can hold the paper's 7 and 6 only if at least 5 mice gave cells to both groups. The Methods allow that ("Recordings in DCZ alone were avoided after >1 DCZ + mCherry experiment per day"), so mice were shared across conditions. Ages at recording are compared with the Methods (injected "when 4-8 weeks old", recorded "3-6 weeks following initial injection") in the next cell, under two readings: whole weeks (49 to 98 days) and up to the end of the eighth and sixth weeks (28 to 62 days at injection, 21 to 48 days later, so 49 to 110 days).

The files are sampled at 20 kHz, where the Methods state digitization at 10 kHz. Neighbouring samples are equal as often within the pairs (2k, 2k+1) as across them, so the 20 kHz samples are not repeated 10 kHz samples. That test alone cannot exclude interpolation from 10 kHz, so each half of the samples was also fitted, by least squares, on the 16 nearest samples of the other half. On the even samples of the same sweeps upsampled back to 20 kHz by linear, cubic or band-limited (FFT) interpolation and rounded, the smaller residual is near the rounding error of the integer samples (0.30 to 0.57 counts, printed above); in the stored data both residuals lie between 0.87 and 1.58 counts in every file and are nearly equal. The test uses the first sweep of each file and these three interpolators; an upsampling it does not model, such as one that adds noise, is not excluded. The result is consistent with acquisition at 20 kHz, and the measures below use the stored rate. Each file is one continuous run of 5-s sweeps with no gap between sweeps (every interval between sweep starts is 5 s), so the time of a sweep within the recording is its index times 5 s. The stimulus series holds only four levels (-150, -100, 0 and +500 pA): it gives the ramp as a step to +500 pA. The eight mice were 53 to 107 days old at recording by their dates of birth. Two, PK-109 and PK-110, at 101 and 107 days, are older than whole weeks would allow (98 days) but within the 110 days the Methods allow if "4-8 weeks old" and "3-6 weeks" run to the end of the eighth and sixth weeks, so the ages are consistent with the Methods.

Channel 1 is stored as a membrane potential series in volts, but it reads -99.8 pA during the -100 pA step, -149.9 pA from 1.0 to 1.1 s, and then a ramp: it is the injected current, in amperes. The current is held at -150 pA for 100 ms before the ramp, which the Methods do not mention. In 40 cells the ramp runs from -150 pA at 1.1 s to +500 pA at 3.1 s, as the Methods state (-150 to +500 pA across 2 s). In the 10 cells listed above (eight of the nine recorded on 2024-08-07, one on 2024-07-24 and one on 2024-07-26) it reaches +500 pA at 2.7 s or 2.5 s, a steeper ramp over 1.6 s or 1.4 s, the same in every sweep of the cell. The stored stimulus shows none of this: it is the same step to +500 pA in every file. Rheobase is therefore read from channel 1, where it agrees with the fitted ramp of each sweep and, in the 40 cells with the nominal ramp, with the Methods' ramp formula, both printed above. A cell's rheobase depends on the ramp's slope, so the ten cells with a steeper ramp are not comparable with the others on rheobase without correction; in a within-cell change the slope is constant. Five sweeps fire in the first 100 ms of the ramp, at -147.5 to -112.3 pA (printed above); the rule takes their first action potential as it comes. A test of rheobase would have to decide whether these sweeps count, as they would pull a cell's rheobase down.

Before any injection channel 1 reads 0.47 to 0.56 pA, so either no holding current was applied or the channel does not include it; the Methods say holding current was adjusted so that each cell began at -65 mV, and 49 of 50 cells have a first-sweep RMP within 3 mV of -65 mV. Within a cell the channel 1 baseline varies by at most a few hundredths of a pA (printed above), so if channel 1 includes the holding current, the holding current is near zero and constant; if it does not, the files hold no record of it. Whether the holding current was constant, which the criterion of fig4j-rheobase-increase asks the author to show, therefore cannot be shown from the files. Channel 1 steps down at the same sample (0.50005 s) in every sweep, and the voltage falls across that moment (median -7.1 mV; 1 of 12858 sweeps by less than 1 mV) and not in the 6 ms before it (median 0.0 mV), so voltage and current share the sweep's clock. The sweep clock cannot be related to a drug application, as no application time is recorded (next cell).

d = sweeps.rheo_A2_pa - sweeps.rheo_A1_pa
both = sweeps.t_ap_A1.notna() & sweeps.t_ap_A2.notna()
for label, sel in [("all sweeps", sweeps.rmp_mv.notna()), ("sweeps with RMP at or below -50 mV", sweeps.rmp_mv <= ps.RMP_MAX_MV)]:
    a1, a2 = sweeps.t_ap_A1.notna() & sel, sweeps.t_ap_A2.notna() & sel
    print(f"{label} ({int(sel.sum())}): first action potential under A1 {int(a1.sum())}, under A2 {int(a2.sum())}, "
          f"A2 only {int((a2 & ~a1).sum())}, A1 only {int((a1 & ~a2).sum())}")
ok = both & (sweeps.rmp_mv <= ps.RMP_MAX_MV)
print("Rheobase A2 - A1 per sweep where both detect, pA; all sweeps:", d[both].describe().round(2).to_dict())
print("  sweeps with RMP at or below -50 mV:", d[ok].describe().round(2).to_dict())
print("Sweeps with RMP at or below -50 mV where A2 comes more than 10 pA before A1:", int((d[ok] < -10).sum()),
      "| more than 10 pA after A1:", int((d[ok] > 10).sum()), "| within 1 pA:", int((d[ok].abs() <= 1).sum()), "of", int(ok.sum()))

A2 (dV/dt above 20 V/s) and A1 (upward crossing of 0 mV) are compared above, sweep by sweep. Among the 11839 sweeps with RMP at or below -50 mV, the two rules give a rheobase within 1 pA of each other in 10335 of the 10675 sweeps where both detect an event, and A2 detects an event in 456 sweeps where A1 detects none. Where A2 comes more than 10 pA earlier (335 sweeps, 325 of them in cells 2024_08_07_0022 and 2024_08_07_0012), its first event peaks at a median of -15.2 mV, and the events A2 alone detects peak between -19.7 and -0.1 mV: these are fast spikes that do not reach 0 mV, which A1 misses, and they are concentrated in a few cells (printed above). In the first 100 ms of the ramp, where the cell is held near -150 pA, A2 finds 7 first events; 5 peak above 0 mV, like the 5 of A1, and 2 peak at -49.3 and -55.8 mV, which are not action potentials: there A2 picks up a fast deflection. The mean rheobase per cell differs between the rules by a median of 0.14 pA, and by up to 336 pA in one cell. No claim is tested, so this decides no outcome; if the conditions were known, rheobase under A2 and A1 would differ in these few cells.

No file names a drug, a condition, a time of application, an expression level or a preincubation. The scan reads every attribute of every object in every file, all sweeps included, and every string dataset of any length, including the text columns of the intracellular recording tables. No file has an /intervals group (no epochs, trials or time intervals), and /analysis and /processing are empty (path list above). Every sweep's series carries the same description ("Response to: ramp" or "Stim type: ramp"), the stimulus description "N/A" and the comment "no comments"; the session description is the same generic sentence in every file, and the experimenter, lab and institution are "_". The dandiset metadata names the two conditions only in its description. Without a condition per cell and a DCZ onset per recording, the comparisons of Fig. 4i,j and Extended Data Fig. 12b cannot be made.

Measures and exclusions for the blocked slice claims¶

The claims are blocked, so this section tests none of them. It computes the per-sweep measures and the exclusions of the Methods (as pager_slice documents, with the readings the criterion of fig4i-rmp-hyperpolarization names) for all 50 cells, so that the number of cells the paper's rules keep can be set against the paper's 41 (reading (b) of methods-slice-sample), and shows the time course of each cell. Which cells belong to which condition, and where DCZ was applied, the files do not say.

methods-slice-sample: The slice data comprise 15 cells from 7 mice recorded with DCZ alone and 26 cells from 6 mice recorded with DCZ plus mCherry.

Result: blocked. Under reading (a) the dataset has 50 cells from 8 mice; under reading (b), with either Rin window and either detection rule, one cell (from PK-113, first-sweep Rin 525 megaohms) is excluded and 49 cells from 8 mice remain, against the paper's 41 cells in total from 7 and 6 mice. Neither reading can be split into the two conditions, because no file records which condition a cell was in, so the four counts the claim states cannot be formed. The totals alone already rule out "reproduced" under both readings: no split of 50 or 49 cells gives 15 and 26. This assumes that every deposited cell was recorded in one of the two conditions, as the dandiset's description names only these two; if some cells were in neither, 41 of them could still split as 15 and 26. Had the conditions been recorded, the outcome could only have been partially or not reproduced, depending on the mouse counts. The 8 or 9 extra cells are not explained by any exclusion the paper states.

The time courses show each cell over a recording of 15.5 to 26 minutes. Without the application time, a change "upon 2-min DCZ addition" cannot be measured, and without the condition the change cannot be compared between groups. The recording order per day is printed because the Methods tie the DCZ-alone recordings to the start of a day; that rule does not say which cells were DCZ alone, so it is not used to assign conditions.

Summary¶

Claim Outcome
methods-slice-sample Blocked: metadata insufficient. 50 cells from 8 mice; no condition per cell
methods-mcherry-preincubation Blocked: data missing. No preincubation times in the files
fig4i-rmp-hyperpolarization Blocked: metadata insufficient. No condition per cell, no DCZ onset
fig4j-rheobase-increase Blocked: metadata insufficient. No condition per cell, no DCZ onset
ed12b-input-resistance-trend Blocked: metadata insufficient. No condition per cell, no DCZ onset
ed12cd-expression-baseline Blocked: data missing. No mEGFP intensity or image per cell
ed12ef-expression-shift Blocked: data missing. No mEGFP intensity or image per cell
ed12g-expression-rmp Blocked: data missing. No mEGFP intensity or image per cell
24 claims on culture, imaging and biochemical data Blocked: data missing. Not in the dandiset, and the paper deposited no other data

How the analysis differs from the paper's: no claim was tested. The per-sweep measures follow the Methods with the readings the claims file names; rheobase is read from channel 1, the current monitor, because the stored stimulus gives the ramp as a step. The two detection rules give a rheobase within 1 pA in 10335 of 10675 sweeps; they differ in a few cells whose spikes do not reach 0 mV, and A2 takes 2 small deflections early in the ramp for action potentials (data check).

What was found about the dataset:

  • No file records the condition of a cell (DCZ alone or DCZ plus mCherry), the time DCZ was applied, the mEGFP intensity of the cell, or the mCherry preincubation time. No file has an intervals group or notes or pharmacology fields, and the session description is generic.
  • The files hold 50 cells from 8 mice; the paper reports 41 cells (15 and 26) from 7 and 6 mice. The extra cells are not marked, and the cells the paper's Rin rule keeps are counted above. Neither total can give the paper's 15 and 26.
  • Channel 1 of every sweep is stored as a CurrentClampSeries in volts but holds the injected current in amperes.
  • The stimulus series gives the ramp (-150 to +500 pA over 2 s) as a step to +500 pA; only channel 1 shows the ramp. In 10 of 50 cells the delivered ramp reaches +500 pA after 1.6 s or 1.4 s, where the Methods state 2 s, and the stimulus series does not show it. Every sweep holds -150 pA for 100 ms before the ramp, which the Methods do not describe.
  • The paper's initial Rin exclusion keeps 49 of the 50 cells, not the 41 the paper analysed; the files do not mark which cells the paper left out, or why.
  • The files are sampled at 20 kHz; the Methods state 10 kHz. The samples are not repeated, and they do not behave like 10 kHz samples upsampled by linear, cubic or band-limited interpolation, which is consistent with acquisition at 20 kHz.
  • Whether the holding current was constant cannot be shown: channel 1 reads about 0.5 pA before any injection, so it either does not include the holding current or none was applied.
  • Experimenter, lab and institution are "_", and the electrodes and device have no description.
